claims.statement: The `sast` job in guardrails.yml is keyless and runs on every push/PR with no `paths:` filter, executing in order: toolchain install (uv, Rust/cargo-audit, pnpm), `uv sync` of each of the four Python surfaces, `check-sast-findings.mjs --selftest`, `sast-scan.mjs --test-rules`, `sast-scan.mjs` (`--scope changed --base <ref>` on pull requests, `--scope full` on push), `check-sast-findings.mjs`, then an always-run upload of the `sast-report` artifact.

The blocking rule is `severity ∈ {High, Critical} AND (kind == sast OR scope == runtime)`, implemented by `deriveBlocking`; dependency scope is computed per ecosystem while SCA always scans the full graph regardless of what changed, because a newly published advisory can hit an unchanged dependency.

All four scanners' native severities are normalized to Critical/High/Medium/Low by the orchestrator via security/sast/severity-map.yaml, and an unmapped native severity is a hard error with no silent default; unscored cargo/pip advisories map to High and cargo informational warnings to Low.

Allowlist suppression requires scanner equality, id equality and a `locationPattern` regex matching the finding's location, plus non-empty `justification` and `addedBy`; a blank required field or an invalid regex raises a GateError (exit 2). Suppression is gate-only — allowlisted findings remain visible in the report and are printed as `allowlisted by <addedBy>`.

Allowlist expiry classification has two inclusive boundaries — an entry exactly 14 days out is already `expiring` and an entry suppresses through the whole of its expiry day — and is computed on UTC date boundaries from a `today` argument rather than the local clock, so a runner timezone or DST transition cannot reclassify an entry. Only `expired` stops suppression.

`WARNING_WINDOW_DAYS = 14` in scripts/allowlist-expiry.mjs is the single definition of the expiry warning window, imported by both the SAST and infra-image gates; the report-only `EXPIRING SOON` / `EXPIRED` / `UNMATCHED ENTRIES` sections never move the normal run's exit code, while the dedicated `--check-expiring` mode runs weekly (Friday) in infra-image-scan and is never run on pull requests.

Unmatched-entry detection only considers entries whose scanner produced at least one finding in the run, so a skipped, failed or clean scanner never flags its whole entry set, and entry identity is a caller-supplied positional key (`<index>:<scanner>:<id>`) rather than the advisory id because one id can appear in several entries.

pip-audit audits the installed venv of each of four registered Python surfaces (PYTHON_SURFACES in scripts/sast-scan.mjs), each deriving its own dependency and runtime sets so a server's package is never classified against another project's graph; any surface failing fails the whole scan and an unsynced venv is a real fault, not a retried transport error.

Two static, finding-independent checks protect the pip-audit surface model at scan time: `assertKnownPythonSurfaces` fails the scan when a Python project directory carrying a `uv.lock` is not registered in `PYTHON_SURFACES`, and `assertPipAuditAllowlistShape` fails the scan when an anchored (`^`-prefixed) `locationPattern` names a surface that does not exist.

Since feature 068 a pip-audit finding's location is project-qualified (`<project>:<pkg>@<version>`), so an anchored allowlist pattern suppresses exactly one surface and an unanchored one deliberately spans all of them.

Semgrep cannot run without egress to its public rule registry (semgrep.dev), which serves the five `p/*` community packs at scan time; when blocked it fails closed and leaves an empty findings.json that the gate passes at exit 0, so a Semgrep green must be sanity-checked with a reachability probe and a `--only semgrep` run, and the committed egress-allowlist entry alone does not prove the host-side per-sandbox policy has been re-applied.

Because a 0-finding report and a 0-blocking-finding report print the same green, the SCA half remains verifiable inside the devcontainer via `--only` (pnpm-audit, cargo-audit and pip-audit reach sources the egress allowlist already permits), which is how a dependency-floor remediation should be checked before pushing.

The gate prints an advisory-only `OVERRIDE LEVERS` section naming whether a finding is cleared by refreshing the lockfile or by raising an override floor; the lever logic lives in the pure scripts/override-lever.mjs module, returns nothing rather than guessing on unreadable input, and never influences the exit code or filters advice by blocking status.

Every keyed entry in pnpm-workspace.yaml's `overrides:` map is a range keyed on a range, so raising the value without moving the key leaves an override that reads as remediated while no longer excluding the vulnerable span; Renovate's npm manager cannot rewrite the key half, and scripts/check-override-consistency.mjs runs on pull requests and fails a mismatched pair by name (plain pins without a key half are out of scope).

Three of the four scanners depend on a third party over the network (pip-audit on osv.dev, cargo-audit on the RustSec advisory DB, pnpm audit on the npm registry), and since item #449 a transient failure is classified against a narrow signature list and retried 3 times with 2 s/4 s exponential backoff before the fail-closed verdict; an unrecognised fault is treated as real and fails on the first attempt.

Transient transport signatures are deliberately anchored: HTTP-status phrases require the status code (item #495) and `Read timed out` requires its terminating period (item #499), because the bare forms also occur in advisory titles and would have retried and then reported a genuine finding anyway.

The transient classification and bounded-retry mechanism is shared between sast-scan.mjs and infra-image-scan.mjs rather than copied, because the signature list is the hard part and a signature learned from one scanner's outage is what the other needs next; that module also owns tail-truncation of scanner output so an HTTP status is not cut off.

A Semgrep rule that could not run appears only in `errors[]`, contributes zero findings, and its allowlist entry surfaces as UNMATCHED — indistinguishable from a remediation — so sast-scan.mjs groups errors by rule into `scanners[].blindedRules` (reading the error message as well as `rule_id`, since PartialParsing errors carry the rule name only in prose) and the gate prints an advisory `RULES THAT COULD NOT RUN` section that annotates the matching UNMATCHED entry.

The custom text-level rule `mcm-ci-curl-pipe-shell` replaces the blinded community rule for the same pattern using `pattern-regex`/`pattern-not-regex` (no sub-parser, so the ci-log-step heredoc is irrelevant), and it names the accepted pinned installer URLs itself rather than accepting them in allowlist.yaml, because an allowlist entry keys on `path:line` and would either be line-pinned or suppress a new `curl | sh` unexamined.

`--scope changed` builds an explicit Semgrep target list filtered by `isScanTarget()` and re-applies the `.semgrepignore` exclusions by hand, so a rule's own `paths:` cannot widen what a pull request is gated on; the filter admits code extensions plus both workflow trees and Dockerfile spellings, and deliberately not every `.yml`, which would pull compose files, Komodo syncs and the security config tree into a PR-scoped scan.

Dockerfiles were invisible to `--scope changed` (item #426), so a PR adding one was gated on nothing and `main` reddened only on the post-merge full scan; the durable answer is the standing `GATE-SCOPE ASYMMETRY` check, which lists blocking SAST findings whose paths are not scan targets (counting allowlisted ones too, excluding SCA, requiring a `generatedAtScope` of `full`, and refusing a missing scope as a GateError) and fails the gate on its own exit path with the remedy of widening the changed-scope filter rather than adding an allowlist entry.

The PR-visible surface was enumerated once by testing every full-scan finding path against `isScanTarget`: after Dockerfiles were admitted, zero blocking findings sit on a file class a pull request cannot see, and the two remaining invisible classes (renovate.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml) are recorded rather than closed because all 22 of their findings are Medium and report-only on a push too — a residual that holds only for the rule set configured today.

`sast-scan.mjs --test-rules` runs `semgrep --test` over security/sast/rules/ ahead of the real scan and additionally fails on any custom rule with no fixture, because `semgrep --test` skips unfixtured rules silently while still printing `N/N ✓`; a code rule's fixture shares its stem while a YAML rule's fixture must be `<rule>.test.yml` so it is not loaded as a second rule.

`--check-expiring` runs inside infra-image-scan, which never produces a SAST report, so check-sast-findings.mjs announces the ENOENT, synthesises `{ findings: [], reportAbsent: true }` and lets the expiry classification run from the allowlist alone; a report that exists but is unparseable is still exit 2, and the absent-report marker — never a merely missing scope — is what the asymmetry check exempts.

Allowlist `locationPattern`s are matched against locations normalized to forward slashes so one pattern works on the Windows dev host and the Linux CI runner; a backslash pattern matches nothing on the runner while passing locally.

cargo-audit is installed fresh on every CI run with a pinned version (`--locked --version 0.22.2`) because `actions/cache` is not mirrored on the self-hosted runner and `--locked` alone locks the tool's dependencies rather than the tool itself.
